From: Alice Turner <alice.turner@bluecrest.com>

Cc: procurement@bluecrest.com
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG follow-up — encryption / key custody artifacts

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BlueCrest’s security review is moving quickly. We finished the SIG questionnaire and the reviewers asked for a short packet showing how Redwood handles customer-managed keys, HSM attestations, and a sample of rotation logs tied to a tenant-managed KMS workflow.

Specifically they asked for:
- A short attestation or cert indicating HSM model, vendor attestation date (if available), and whether Redwood uses an external HSM provider or cloud-managed HSM.
- Example rotation logs showing an emergency rotation and a regular monthly rotation (redacted, but timestamps and actor IDs should be preserved).
- Network segmentation diagram showing where key management endpoints live relative to inference nodes.
- Short notes on in-transit encryption (TLS versions, mutual TLS for private links) and at-rest disk encryption for model artifacts.

Can you send a single package or point me to a drive folder? We need to include these artifacts in our SIG upload by EOD Monday (2027-06-02). If any items require an NDA or additional paperwork, flag it and we can route to procurement.

Thanks,
Alice Turner
Security Engineer | BlueCrest Technologies
alice.turner@bluecrest.com

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — encryption / key custody artifacts

Alice — thanks for the patience. Attached is the packet we assembled for your SIG upload. Quick summary below and attachments included:

Summary:
- HSM attestation: Redwood uses cloud-provider managed HSM (FIPS 140-2 L3 equivalent in provider environment). We maintain a vendor attestation PDF from CloudHSM Inc., dated 2027-04-30 (attached: hsm-attestation-2027-04-30.pdf).
- Rotation logs: sample redacted rotation CSV showing periodic and emergency rotations; no secret material included (attached: redwood-kms-rotation-log-sample.csv).
- Network diagram: segmentation image showing KMS/control-plane boundaries and inference clusters; public endpoints are behind WAF and transit traffic uses mTLS for Dedicated/Private links (attached: redwood-network-segmentation-diagram.png).
- TLS & at-rest: Redwood requires TLS1.2+ for public hosted API and TLS1.3 preferred. For private deployments we support mutual TLS and customer-managed certificates. All persistent storage for model artifacts and KV caches is AES-256 at rest, with disk encryption keys managed by the cloud provider. We have optional envelope encryption using customer KEKs for Dedicated/Private (documented in the BYOK runbook).

Attachments included in this email: redwood-kms-rotation-log-sample.csv; hsm-attestation-2027-04-30.pdf; redwood-network-segmentation-diagram.png

Note on additional items: We can provide an internal access matrix mapping actor IDs to persons/services, but that requires an NDA amendment to include names. If BlueCrest prefers, we can deliver the mapping via secure Drive share with time-limited access.

Please confirm receipt and whether you want the files zipped or uploaded into your SIG portal directly. If you need a labeled cover letter for the SIG upload, laura and i can draft a one-page sign-off.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
